statement: Phase 0.3 locking reads use one deterministic fail-fast reservation-conflict policy: the partition transaction participant owns acquire/conflict/release of durable replicated reservations, DistributedTransactionCoordinator owns transaction lifetime and cross-participant rollback/recovery, a conflicting reservation returns a typed refusal instead of entering a waiter queue, any multi-participant reservation conflict aborts and rolls back the whole transaction so no hold-and-wait state exists, timeout/cancellation/commit/rollback/recovery release through transaction ownership, and deadlock is impossible in the initial slice because no wait graph is created.

constraints.statement: PG wire transports the locking-read semantic only; no PG-session-local mutex, lock map, retry loop or cache is lock authority.
The partition transaction participant is the only owner of reservation acquire/conflict/release at the data owner.
DistributedTransactionCoordinator owns transaction lifetime, participant enlistment, timeout, cancellation, whole-transaction rollback and recovery re-drive.
A reservation held by another transaction produces a typed immediate conflict refusal. Phase 0.3 creates no waiter queue and no wake-up correctness path.
If any participant refuses a reservation, the whole transaction is rolled back and all earlier reservations are released; no transaction retains reservations while waiting on another transaction.
Because the initial slice never waits while holding reservations, there is no wait-for graph and no deadlock detector/timeout-as-deadlock-breaker.
A participant must not independently expire an unresolved reservation on its local clock. Commit, rollback, timeout, cancellation or recovery resolution owns release.
Contention, transaction timeout, cancellation and abort remain distinguishable typed outcomes.
Any future blocking WAIT/NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED policy with waiter wake-up semantics must supersede this seal rather than grow a second authority beside it.
